scope: Corollary 8.4 (Raw extremal-length budgets) of the manuscript “The critical Liouville quantum sphere and geometric limits of FK maps at q=4” (preprints/The-critical-Liouville-quantum-sphere-and-geometric-limits-of-FK-maps-at-q-equals-4-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9b9236021eab20eb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 147. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In every diverging perimeter extraction, the following conclusions hold along the good spatial-comparison subsequences. 1. The family of all curves making a fixed positive spherical advance has extremal length bounded below by a strictly positive constant, eventually along the extraction. 2. For circular rings in an ordinary planar chart, with a fixed comparable-radius ratio and fixed comparable buffer margins, there is a strictly positive lower bound on through extremal length that is uniform in radius and location. For each fixed ring test the bound holds eventually along the extraction; the eventual discrete index may depend on the ring.
